content:
**Visual observations from test image:**
- Close-up of a soybean petiole that is prominently dark brown to reddish-brown/almost black along its full length
- Hairy texture still visible on the petiole
- Leaves are mostly green with only minor small spots

**Candidate narrowing:**
- Diaporthe: brown lesions on petioles/stems, black pycnidia — matches the dark petiole discoloration seen
- Anthracnose: brown cankers on petioles causing defoliation — also plausible
- Stem Canker: reddish-brown lesions at base of branches/petioles

The Diaporthe reference (bottom-left quadrant) shows very similar brown petiole discoloration on soybean plants. The dark, uniform browning of the petiole in the test image is characteristic of Diaporthe pod and stem blight affecting petioles at later growth stages.
